title: Generic Qualitative Coding
short_description: General-purpose qualitative analysis guidance for preparing a corpus, reading closely, coding, memo-writing, comparison, synthesis, and reporting.

phases.title: Preparing corpus
phases.description: Clarify the research focus, document inclusion criteria, and organize the corpus before detailed analysis.
prompts: Why does this document belong in the corpus?
What context is needed to interpret this text responsibly?
What is missing from the current corpus?

phases.title: Close reading
phases.description: Read slowly for meaning, context, repetition, contradiction, and surprising details.
prompts: What stands out in this passage?
What assumptions does the text invite?
Which words or phrases deserve coding?
recommended_actions: Avoid coding entire documents when a passage is enough.

phases.title: Open coding
phases.description: Create provisional labels for patterns, actions, meanings, and topics in the data.
prompts: What is this passage about?
What action, process, value, or problem is visible?
What code name would remain understandable later?

phases.title: Memo-writing
phases.description: Use memos to capture interpretations, uncertainties, methodological decisions, and emerging arguments.
prompts: What do I think this means?
What evidence supports this interpretation?
What alternative interpretation should be kept open?
recommended_actions: Link memos to codes, documents, or segments.
Mark important memos for later synthesis.

phases.title: Comparison
phases.description: Compare segments, codes, documents, and cases to refine distinctions and patterns.
prompts: How is this instance similar to earlier instances?
How is it different?
Does this comparison split, merge, or redefine a code?
recommended_actions: Look for negative or deviant cases.

phases.title: Analytical synthesis
phases.description: Move from coded material toward claims, explanations, and evidence-backed conclusions.
prompts: Which codes form a larger pattern?
What evidence is strongest?
What claim can be made without overstating the data?
recommended_actions: Use relations to connect evidence and claims.

phases.title: Export/reporting
phases.description: Prepare transparent outputs for reporting codes, evidence, memos, and methodological decisions.
prompts: Can another reader follow the analytical procedure?
Which exports document the evidence chain?
Which protocol decisions should be reported?
What is the research question asking me to notice?
What evidence supports this interpretation?
What methodological decision should be documented?

concepts.description: A clear statement of when and why a code should be applied.
prompts: When should this code be used?
What should be excluded?

concepts.description: A case or passage that complicates, contradicts, or limits an emerging claim.
prompts: What does this case challenge?
Should the claim be revised?

sources.apa: Saldaña, J. (2021). The coding manual for qualitative researchers (4th ed.). SAGE.
sources.note: Use for coding cycles, code definitions, analytic memoing, and reporting.

sources.apa: Miles, M. B., Huberman, A. M., & Saldaña, J. (2020). Qualitative data analysis: A methods sourcebook (4th ed.). SAGE.
sources.note: Use for qualitative data displays, analytic condensation, and evidence-based conclusions.
